osu_azvhouse.t: Arizona v. House of Representatives, No. 1:25-cv-03740 (D.D.C.) — Ohio State Election Law case tracker

checks.legal: CourtListener and Justia could not be searched directly: the network proxy refuses both hosts and the fetch tool refuses unsearched URLs (Oct. 14, 2026). A site-restricted web search of courtlistener.com/justia.com was run instead, plus news searches. Site-restricted search and news searches found only the 2025 suit in which she was a plaintiff (below). No case against her.
checks.foreign: House candidate (May 2025) and new-filer (Aug. 2026) reports read directly: no foreign assets, gifts or travel. FARA: exact-name search of the FARA bulk files (registrants, short forms, foreign principals), Oct. 13, 2026: no match.
checks.claims: Campaign homepage refused by fetch tool. Mechanical sample = every checkable claim in the campaign's announcement release (her bio) plus her first-week House press release. 8 rated: 6 true, 2 unverifiable. No 2026 ads found in coverage.
checks.democracy: Not in Congress for any certification count (sworn in Nov. 2025). NOTE: the records profile's six 'Grijalva' certification votes (2005 Ohio objection Yea; 2021 Arizona/Pennsylvania Nay) are her father Raul Grijalva's votes and were deliberately NOT attributed to her.

legal.t: Joined Arizona as co-plaintiff in a D.D.C. suit (No. 1:25-cv-03740) against the House, its Clerk and Sergeant-at-Arms seeking a declaration that she must be sworn in; she was the plaintiff, not a defendant.
legal.status: Voluntarily dismissed by all plaintiffs, Nov. 14, 2025

research_notes: Records-profile 'cert' entries belong to Raul Grijalva (father), matched by surname only; fix the profile mapping. Courts news-only (CourtListener/Justia blocked).
